summary: The design can physically reach M2, most plausibly on qkv m=128, which replaces two cuBLAS nodes (16.0 us). It has two concrete defects to fix before building. First, the qkv 2x7 (and 1x7 fallback) cluster cannot be co-resident in one wave on 132 SMs at 1 CTA/SM, and the brief's 'max active clusters == 0' test does not catch that. Second, the DSMEM epilogue moves 6-14 MB per launch, several times the 1-1.5 us budget. Dispatch as an okc check once the two in-flight cluster/DSMEM checks have at least reported build and self-check status.
justification: Incumbents (master 1602a4e947e64090, untouched by the restack at m>=128): qkv m=128 row 16.81 (nvjet splitK 13.0 + splitKreduce 3.0), qkv m=256 19.62/19.4, pooler m=128 25.55/25.7, pooler m=256 30.53/29.5, unpooler m=128 19.79/20.4. The hypothesis quotes all of these correctly, its expected directions match the TASK floors, and its untouched shapes are correctly marked flat. Mechanism: swap-AB with T=256 gives a 128x256 CTA tile. That is 1.33x the arithmetic intensity of the 128x128 tiles that failed. Multicasting x across the pair halves the x L2->SM re-read that REWRITE_READ section 1 named as the ceiling. Real WS plus setmaxnreg is what Triton 3.8 could not deliver. So the change is more than a re-skin. Two caveats. (i) At m=128 the T=128 tile is the same 128x128 product tile as the failed attempts, only transposed, so the m=128 gain must come from multicast plus the single-node reduce, not from the tile. (ii) The best prior for a hand-written WS wgmma kernel is CUTLASS's own (job f5b1361aaa0e48b5: 128x128x64, cluster 2x1 multicast, cooperative WS). With NO split-K (unpooler m=256, Heuristic/DataParallel) it ran 26.8 us at 608 TFLOP/s, against nvjet's 24.6. Pooler m=256 reached 495 TFLOP/s. The '~700 TFLOP/s' behind the qkv m=256 <= 14 and pooler m=256 <= 24 targets is therefore above anything measured here. Per-shape view: qkv m=128 needs only ~500 TFLOP/s plus a <=2 us epilogue to beat 16.0, so it is the likeliest M2 win. Pooler m=128 is mixed-bound (needs ~3.5 TB/s and ~450 TFLOP/s together), which is plausible. Both m=256 rows are long shots in stage 1. WEAKEST LINK, in two parts. (a) Cluster residency. A 2x7=14-CTA cluster at 1 CTA/SM (192 KB smem) fits at most once per GPC. H100/H200 GPCs hold roughly 14-18 SMs, so at most ~8 clusters (112 CTAs) are co-resident, against the 9 clusters (126 CTAs) the grid needs. The 1x7 fallback fits 2 per GPC, so at most ~16 clusters against 18 needed. Either way a second wave roughly doubles qkv time. cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters will return a positive number, so the stated fallback test (== 0) never fires. Pooler's 2x4=8 cluster needs 16 co-resident clusters, which fails if any GPC has fewer than 16 usable SMs. (b) Epilogue bytes. Total DSMEM traffic is about CTAs x tile_fp32 x (S-1)/S: qkv m=256 ~126 x 128 KB x 6/7 ~ 14 MB, pooler m=256 ~12.6 MB, pooler m=128 ~6.3 MB. Published Hopper microbenchmarks put aggregate SM-to-SM throughput around ~3.3 TB/s for the whole GPU, lower for larger clusters. If that holds, the epilogue is 2-4+ us, not 1-1.5 us, and it alone erases the m=256 margin. Fixes to put in the implement brief: (1) in prepare, compute needed_clusters = grid_CTAs / cluster_size, print it next to cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters, and treat max_active < needed as 'does not fit in one wave'. For qkv, choose among single-wave candidates (e.g. 36 token-half x weight tiles at T=128 with S=3 and cluster 2x3; or 18 tiles with S=4 and cluster 2x4, at the cost of fill) and print the one chosen. (2) Build a print-only no-reduce variant (mainloop + local bf16 store of the partial) and print full vs no_reduce cold-L2 times per layer. The m128-wspec read split mainloop from tail the same way, and that split is what makes stage 2 decidable. (3) S=7 does not divide 128 rows: specify an integer row partition, e.g. ceil-split 19/19/18/18/18/18/18. (4) The multicast pair needs the remote empty-barrier protocol: each consumer must arrive on BOTH CTAs' empty mbarrier (mapa + mbarrier.arrive.shared::cluster) before the issuing producer reuses that slot. Missing it is a silent, intermittent race that a 2-run bit-identity check may not catch.
confounders: sglang-gemm-dispatch-parity: defines the cuBLAS fallback that is the incumbent on every routed shape. The new route sits in front of it, so there is no interaction on kernel time. cuBLAS m>=128 rows swing up to ~7% between runs (pooler m=128 nvjet 23.9 vs 25.7), so judge against the in-prepare side-by-side cold-L2 cuBLAS time and the 1602 profile, not against one row.
router-triton-hilo-fused-control-splitk-all-m: owns the router at m=128/256 in the same loads, a separate graph per shape. No shared kernel or memory; it only moves the load-level headline.

bf16-m32-swapab-wgmma-triton / bf16-shape-gated-triton-winners-combo: m<=32 only; disjoint shapes. They matter only if the routing gate is written as an elif chain that changes their m bounds, so keep separate bound constants (LESSONS 2026-10-25 stack lesson).
interference: No companion. This is stage 1 of a rewrite, judged on the replaced kernels' own time in top_kernels plus the prepare diagnostics, and no landed hypothesis shares its shapes or code path. What decides stage 2 is internal: mainloop vs epilogue (the no-reduce print) and wave count (cluster residency print). Both belong in this run as print-only diagnostics, not as extra checks. On the in-flight checks: router-cuda-cluster-dsmem-splitk-rewrite (dc5d03c4d9604b0e) and o-unpooler-slice-cuda-cluster-dsmem-rewrite (3f3330f70b6e4cdc) are the first judge runs of the shared machinery: load_inline + cudaLaunchKernelEx cluster attribute, mapa/ld.shared::cluster, and barrier.cluster arrive.release/wait.acquire. A fault there poisons the context (LESSONS), and the same bug would kill this run. So WAIT for their logs (build OK, cluster launch accepted, max-active-clusters print, self-check pass or fault) before dispatching, and fold any fix into this kernel. Do NOT wait for their performance verdicts. They reduce tiny [16,NT] partials over portable clusters of 8 with mma.sync and no TMA, so they say nothing about the epilogue bandwidth (64-128 KB per CTA), non-portable cluster sizes, TMA multicast, wgmma or setmaxnreg, which are this run's real risks.
rules_flags: None blocking. Weight TMA descriptors built in prepare derive from weights (allowed). The x descriptor is rebuilt per call from pointer and m, so nothing derived from data is cached. Ensure the host-side cuTensorMapEncodeTiled call happens during capture and reads no tensor values.

Every timed call is checked, but no judge TEST passes through this route: m=130 unpooler and m=512 qkv both stay on master. Correctness therefore rests on the in-prepare self-check. Add a 'dist outliers'-style x (a few rows scaled by 2^8-2^12) to it alongside the one-hot probe.
Keep wgmma/setmaxnreg under __CUDA_ARCH_FEAT_SM90_ALL with #error in the #else, and grep the log for the arch print, build OK and PATH CHOSEN before reading any number (LESSONS 2026-10-25).
open_questions: What does cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters return on the judge for 14, 8, 7, 6 and 4 CTA clusters at ~192 KB smem? This decides the qkv and pooler decompositions. Print all of them in prepare regardless of which is launched.
Is the DSMEM epilogue bandwidth-bound? Compare full vs no_reduce per layer, and if it exceeds ~1.5 us, consider in stage 2 a smaller S, or 64-row weight tiles with T=256 and no split.

Is the T=256 consumer (m64n256 per warpgroup, 128 fp32 accumulator regs/thread at setmaxnreg 232) spill-free? Print the spill line and do not trust a run that spills (LESSONS 2026-10-25: 'a wgmma build that runs is not a fast one').
